official.deadline_note: The 14 April 2027 date is the Foundation's own application deadline on its platform. University application deadlines at the approved South African institutions are separate and earlier, and a place must be secured by January of the year in residence or the scholarship cannot be taken up.
official.application_cycle: Class of 2028 intake: applications open Tuesday 9 March 2027 and close Wednesday 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2. The Foundation states its applications timeline runs from March to November of each year for the following year's intake.
official.status_note: The official page states that applications for 2027 are now closed and that applications for the Class of 2028 will open on Tuesday 9 March 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition and registration fees as set by the scholar's university or institution, paid directly to the tertiary institution.
benefits: Tuition and registration fees as set by your university or institution
A study materials allowance as set by the MRF
Accommodation and meal allowances as set by the MRF
A medical aid allowance and a personal allowance as set by the MRF
Research and conferencing grants, which can be made available on request
Economy-class flights for international scholars from their home countries to their institutions at the start and end of their studies
eligibility: I can study at a postgraduate level in English (the Foundation offers a free self-check English test for those unsure)
I am a citizen of an African country, no matter where I am currently living or studying
I am between the ages of 19 and 29 in the year of applying, and younger than 30 at the time of taking up the Scholarship
By 1 Jan 2028, I will have an undergraduate degree with excellent academic results (above 70% or upper-second class Honours)
The scholarship is for postgraduate study only - an Honours or a Master's degree; undergraduate study is not funded
requirements: You must apply online, uploading your documents and essays on the Foundation's applications platform
Three letters of recommendation, in English, submitted by the recommenders directly through the platform - without these letters you cannot submit your application
Upload certificates of completion for your degrees
Upload transcripts of your academic results, in English
Upload scans of your ID and passport documents
Write two short essays: one on your personal journey, and one on a specific question relating to the Foundation's principles
State your proposed course of study; proof of having applied to a university is not required
documents: Three letters of recommendation in English, uploaded by the recommenders on the platform
Certificates of completion for your degrees
Transcripts of your academic results, in English
Scans of your ID and passport documents
Two short essays (personal journey; a question relating to the Foundation's principles)
selection_criteria: Aspiration to the principles of leadership, reconciliation, education and entrepreneurship, with demonstrated potential to live them out
A combination of intellect and character: marks above 70% or an upper second
Demonstrated leadership on your campus or in your community
Progression through screening rounds - Round Two (notified by mid-July), Round Three (end of July) and a Final Round interview in South Africa in October
coverage: Tuition and registration fees as set by the institution, paid directly to the tertiary institution
Allowances as set by the MRF for study materials, accommodation and meals, medical aid and personal spending
Research and conferencing grants on request
Economy-class travel for international scholars from home to their institution at the beginning and end of the degree
Transport to leadership workshops organised and paid for by the MRF for scholars not based in the Western Cape
application_method: Register on the Foundation's applications platform when applications open on 9 March 2027
Add three recommenders on the platform and ensure each signs in and uploads their own English letter before the close
Upload degree certificates, English transcripts, ID and passport scans and both essays
State your proposed course of study and submit the complete application by 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2
official.application_route: Apply online only, through the Mandela Rhodes Foundation's applications platform, accessed via mandelarhodes.org once applications open.
official.study_mode: Full-time study only, as set out in the Foundation's terms and conditions
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of an African country are eligible wherever they live or study, but the degree must be taken in person at a recognised South African institution - study in your home country and distance learning are not allowed.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. Students who are citizens of an African country outside South Africa are eligible; final-round applicants based outside South Africa are flown in for the in-person interview, and international scholars receive economy-class travel to and from their home country at the start and end of the degree.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Honours or Master's study in any field at a recognised South African institution of higher education approved by the MRF. The Foundation does not fund MBAs, any type of block course, or courses delivered predominantly online.
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required; the application instead requires two short essays, one on your personal journey and one on a question relating to the Foundation's principles.
official.duration: Funded to a strict maximum of two years: one year of funding for an Honours degree, and one or two years for a Master's degree.
official.description: The Mandela Rhodes Scholarship is a unique opportunity for young leaders from anywhere on the African continent to further their education in South Africa, combining comprehensive funding for the core costs of a one-year Honours or two-year Master's degree in any field at a recognised South African institution with a compulsory leadership development programme built on the Foundation's principles of reconciliation, education, entrepreneurship and leadership.
official.program_type: Foundation postgraduate scholarship (Honours or Master's) with a compulsory leadership development programme
official.english_requirement: You must be able to do written and verbal academic work in English at a postgraduate level; English is the main medium of tuition at South African universities. The Foundation publishes no required IELTS or TOEFL score, noting some universities may require test results.

applicant_utility.summary: The MRF pays tuition and registration directly to your university and pays all other allowances to you twice a year, so plan cash flow around the two payment dates. The award only works if you separately win a place at a South African university, so apply to universities in parallel rather than after the MRF round. The 2028 window is short - applications open 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 - and your submission cannot be completed until all three referees have uploaded their letters on the platform.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African citizens aged 19-29 with a first degree above 70% or an upper-second, evidence of campus or community leadership, and a concrete Honours or Master's plan at one of the approved South African universities.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure three recommenders before applications open on 9 March 2027; each must register on the platform and upload their own English letter, so give them weeks, not days

Prepare degree certificates and transcripts in English, and if your qualifications come from outside South Africa start SAQA verification early - the MRF warns it can take 4-8 weeks and does not cover the cost
Draft both essays (personal journey, and a principles question) before the platform opens, then refine them
Apply to at least two of the approved South African universities as early as possible; acceptance by January of your year in residence is a condition of taking up the award
Budget separately for items the award does not cover: visa, SAQA verification, university application fees, passport, day-to-day transport and personal insurance
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete submissions: no late or incomplete applications are accepted under any circumstances, and a missing referee letter blocks submission entirely
No South African university place by January of the year in residence - a selected applicant who is not accepted cannot take up the scholarship
Academic shortfall: marks below 70% or below an upper second, or foreign qualifications that collide with NQF requirements without SAQA verification
Proposing an MBA, a block course, a predominantly online course or distance learning, all of which are explicitly not funded
Holding another scholarship or funded opportunity, or planning paid work beyond 12 hours per week - both breach the conditions of tenure
Treating the leadership programme as optional: three workshops in year one (plus regional pods) are compulsory, and travel outside South Africa is not accepted as a reason for absence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa application costs, SAQA qualification verification, university application fees, passport or other travel documents, day-to-day local transport, and personal insurance - the MRF funds none of these, and any amount owed before you become a Scholar is your sole responsibility.
document_audit: Certificates and transcripts must be provided in English; anything in another language needs certified translation before upload
Referees must upload their own letters through the platform - letters emailed to you or self-uploaded do not count
ID and passport scans are required at application stage; the MRF will not fund acquiring a passport even if you are flown in for the final-round interview
If your degree is from outside South Africa, expect your chosen universities to ask for SAQA verification - keep the reference and outcome ready for both admission and your study visa
Some universities require their own English proficiency test results even though the MRF does not; check each institution's requirement early
alerts: Applications for the Class of 2028 open 9 March 2027 and close 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2 - a window of roughly five weeks with no extensions
The scholarship cannot be deferred: you must accept it for the year it is offered
A delayed study visa can mean you miss the January start and lose the scholarship - apply as soon as you have university acceptance
You may not hold other scholarships or funded opportunities, and paying work is capped at 12 hours per week
You may not change institution later without explicit MRF approval, so choose your universities deliberately
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register on the MRF applications platform, complete the form and both essays, upload certificates, transcripts and ID/passport scans, add three recommenders who upload their letters, and submit before 14 April 2027 23:59 GMT+2; shortlisting runs through July and August rounds to an in-person Final Round interview in South Africa in October, with selection notified by end of October.
